best_for: 3D printer owners, Prusa or not, who want a free slicer with tested profiles and a direct line to Printables models.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: PrusaSlicer costs nothing and is licensed AGPL-3.0. Prusa says it works with any FDM or resin printer, and ships more than 200 tested profiles for Prusa printers and filaments.

points.title: Printables built in
points.text: A Printables browser inside the app lets you find a model, import it, slice it and send it to the printer. Browsing needs no account.

points.title: Sends jobs over the network
points.text: You can send G-code over the local network, with one click to Klipper and OctoPrint, or through Prusa Connect to watch and start prints remotely. A command-line mode handles batch slicing.

points.title: 2.9 added multiple beds
points.text: Version 2.9.0 brought multiple virtual beds, scarf seams, paint-on fuzzy skin and better handling of several nozzle sizes.

points.title: Update for 2.9.7
points.text: The 2.9.7 release is a small fix for security holes, including bugs that could be triggered by opening a crafted 3MF or binary G-code file. If you open models from strangers, take it.

points.title: Linux means Flathub
points.text: Since 2.9.0, Prusa ships the Linux version only through Flathub, and the 2.9.7 release has no AppImage. The Flathub listing is verified as Prusa's own.

points.title: Windows and Mac notes
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 or later on 64-bit, and the installer sets it up for the whole machine. macOS gets one universal build. The Windows listing keeps 24 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
